context: A draft contractual sentence backed by a percentile computed over a run that spent most of its life below the rate being committed to. Predicted baseline failure: the agent reads the export the way Marco did - p(95) 690 ms against a 1,000 ms budget, dropped_iterations 0, both thresholds ok - and signs both sentences, perhaps tightening a threshold on the way past. The shape of the run is what settles it and it is only visible in the sample file: the scenario ramps for 16 minutes and holds 1,400 requests/second for 4, so 240 of the 300 sampled requests were taken while the offered rate was below the rate in the sentence. Restricted to the last four minutes the 95th percentile is about 2,750 ms - nearly three times the budget - while 690 ms is simply what sixteen minutes of cheap ramp samples produce when they are pooled with it. The second predicted failure is the mirror: pattern-matching on the 880 requests/second in http_reqs and refusing sentence 1 as well. Sentence 1 is true. Nothing was dropped, the pool never bound (vus max 1,642 against maxVUs 2,500), and 880/s is the average of a ramp, not a shortfall. Banding the samples by the arrival rate in force shows where the service actually turns: p95 is 360 ms at 900-1,050/s, 468 ms at 1,050-1,200/s, and 2,697 ms once the run reaches 1,400, so a defensible commitment is near 1,200 requests/second and the honest repair to sentence 2 is either that lower rate or a re-run held at 1,400 for long enough to measure it.

checklist.name: MUST NOT let the latency sentence stand on a whole-run percentile
checklist.description: MUST NOT keep sentence 2 as written, and MUST NOT defend any latency figure for 1,400 requests/second with the 690 ms in the summary or with the fact that the p(95)<1000 threshold reported ok - that statistic pools sixteen minutes of ramp with four minutes at the committed rate. Leaving sentence 2 in place, in any wording, scores zero for this criterion regardless of the rest. Full marks require the corrected document to carry the figure computed over the part of the run that was actually at 1,400/s - the last four minutes, roughly 2.7-2.8 seconds at the 95th percentile - and to say that is the number the sentence would have to survive. Refusing the sentence on general grounds - one run is not enough, pre-production is not production, percentiles are noisy - without restricting the measurement to the committed rate and stating what it gives, scores at most half.

checklist.name: The throughput sentence is not refused as collateral
checklist.description: Sentence 1 is supportable and must survive: dropped_iterations is 0, the run reached its configured 1,400/s, and the virtual-user pool never bound (vus max 1,642 against maxVUs 2,500). Refusing both sentences, or declining to commit to anything from this run, scores zero here - it is the mirror-image failure of signing both. Citing the 880 requests/second in http_reqs as evidence that the platform did not reach 1,400 also scores zero: that average is low because sixteen of the twenty minutes were ramp, and the answer that gets full marks says so.

checklist.name: The check restricts the window before it measures anything
checklist.description: scripts/check-capacity.mjs selects the rows at the rate being committed to before computing any statistic, and refuses the run on that basis, writing reports/capacity-check.json and exiting non-zero on the supplied inputs. A check that computes percentiles over every sampled row, or that only re-reads the threshold ok flags out of the summary, scores zero even if it happens to exit non-zero. reports/capacity-check.json must be the script's own output rather than hand-written, and the reason it gives must be the windowed number rather than a generic failure string.

checklist.name: The run configuration is changed so the committed window is measured on its own
checklist.description: tests/load/api.js is changed so a repeat cannot report clean: the plateau is separated from the ramp so that the sustained portion carries its own pass/fail - distinct scenarios, or a threshold scoped to the sustained stage - and the summary emits statistics past the p(95) the default output stops at. Leaving the options block untouched scores zero. Only lowering the 1000 in p(95)<1000 to a smaller number scores at most half: the statistic is computed over the wrong population, so changing its budget is not the repair.

checklist.name: A defensible rate is put in place of 1,400
checklist.description: The answer names what the run does support - a rate in the region of 1,100-1,200 requests/second, where the sampled 95th percentile is still a few hundred milliseconds - or states that the sentence cannot be made at 1,400 without a re-run held at that rate long enough to measure, and says how long. Rewriting the document to say nothing about capacity at all scores at most half; leaving procurement with only a refusal and no number or path scores zero.

checklist.name: The computation is covered by tests and the suite stays green
checklist.description: test/check-capacity.test.mjs exercises the windowing and the percentile on known input with a hand-checkable expected value - not merely that the function returns an object - and covers a run the check should accept as well as one it should refuse. npm test passes with the pre-existing csv test still green. A suite that does not run scores zero.

checklist.name: Deliverables produced and supplied inputs untouched
checklist.description: docs/capacity-statement.md, scripts/check-capacity.mjs, test/check-capacity.test.mjs and reports/capacity-check.json all exist, and runs/2026-09-08-summary.json, data/samples-2026-09-08.csv, lib/csv.mjs and test/csv.test.mjs are byte-identical to what was supplied. Editing any supplied export or sample file scores zero here.
